title.narrative: Results ChainMaintained functionality of existing health facilities to deliver health services to the population of Gaza to reduce indirect mortality and morbidity during the current escalation of hostilities and after their conclusionSustained management of chronic diseases, communicable disease, and child health (diabetes, hypertension, asthma/COPD). Procurement of medication, diagnostics, consumables and equipment, and where necessary support medical evacuation from Gaza to Egypt.Strengthened mental health and psychosocial services.Further integration of mental health into health facilities, including community MH centres and psychiatric hospital care; providing support for firstline health providers; ensuring support for people with mental disorders, women, children and adolescents, GBV survivors and the elderly, with scalable evidencebased psychological interventionsReactivated key aspects of the health information system, including surveillance.Support of health information systems, analytics and health surveillance through carrying out risk and needs assessment informing prioritization and implementation, health information analytics, and reporting.In line with Overall Objective (OO):Collaborative multistakeholder assessment of health needs and risks, health sector capacities, and operational and political contexts that is informed by the conflict analysis developed (Source: `Bridging the Divide);Collective, concrete and measurable outcomes and results that the humanitarian, development and other relevant actors want to achieve jointly over a multiyear period (Source: `Bridging the Divide); andCollaborative, multistakeholder plan which is either a single plan that covers humanitarian, development and peace needs, or a humanitarian response plan that covers multiple years and is closely aligned to the development plan (Source: `Bridging the Divide).

Procurement of medication, diagnostics, consumables and equipment, and where necessary support medical evacuation from Gaza to Egypt.Strengthened mental health and psychosocial services.Further integration of mental health into health facilities, including community MH centres and psychiatric hospital care; providing support for firstline health providers; ensuring support for people with mental disorders, women, children and adolescents, GBV survivors and the elderly, with scalable evidencebased psychological interventionsReactivated key aspects of the health information system, including surveillance.Support of health information systems, analytics and health surveillance through carrying out risk and needs assessment informing prioritization and implementation, health information analytics, and reporting.In line with Overall Objective (OO):Collaborative multistakeholder assessment of health needs and risks, health sector capacities, and operational and political contexts that is informed by the conflict analysis developed (Source: `Bridging the Divide);Collective, concrete and measurable outcomes and results that the humanitarian, development and other relevant actors want to achieve jointly over a multiyear period (Source: `Bridging the Divide); andCollaborative, multistakeholder plan which is either a single plan that covers humanitarian, development and peace needs, or a humanitarian response plan that covers multiple years and is closely aligned to the development plan (Source: `Bridging the Divide).
